# Judith Chapter 15 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_015_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And when those who were in the tents heard it, they were amazed at what had happened.

**2** And trembling and fear fell upon them, and no man stayed close to his neighbor, but they all broke out together and fled by every path of the plain and the hill country.

**3** And those who had camped in the hill country around Bethulia also turned and fled. And then the sons of Israel, every warrior among them, rushed out upon them.

**4** And Uzziah sent to Betomasthaim and Bebai and Choba and Kola and to every territory of Israel such men as told all that had happened; and all who heard rushed upon the enemy and struck them down.

**5** And Joakim the high priest and the senate of the sons of Israel who dwelt in Jerusalem came down to behold the good things that the LORD had done for Israel and to see Judith and to greet her with peace.

**6** And when they came before her, they all blessed her with one voice and said to her, "You are the exaltation of Jerusalem, you are the great glory of Israel, you are the great pride of our people.

**7** You have done all these things with your hand; you have done good things for Israel, and God is pleased with it. Blessed may you be before the Lord Almighty forever." And all the people said, "Amen."

**8** And all the people plundered the camp for thirty days; and they gave to Judith the tent of Holofernes and all his silver vessels and his beds and his bowls and all his furniture; and she took them and loaded them on her mule and hitched up her wagons and piled them on them.

**9** And all the women of Israel came running to see her, and they blessed her and performed a dance in her honor; and she took branches in her hands and distributed them to the women who were with her.

**10** And they crowned themselves with olive wreaths, she and those with her, and she went before all the people in the dance, leading all the women; and all the men of Israel followed in their armor, with garlands and with songs of praise on their lips.

**11** And Judith sang this song of praise in the presence of all Israel, and all the people raised the voice of this praise aloud.

---
*EMET notes: v. 5 — "senate" (gerousia) same term as ch. 11 — the highest council of Jerusalem comes in person. The high priest Joakim appeared briefly in the early chapters blessing the people. His coming now is the completion of a narrative frame. v. 9 — "performed a dance" (echoreusen) is specific liturgical choreography, not informal dancing. v. 10 — the procession is deliberately structured: Judith leads the women, the armed men follow. The military victory is expressed as a processional psalm. v. 8 — "thirty days" of plunder is a detail establishing the scale of the Assyrian defeat.*
